headline: SOLACE+ lung cancer screening consortium launches in Vienna with 46 partners
dek: The project brings together partners from 22 EU Member States and Norway to scale up lung cancer screening across Europe, building on the original SOLACE project.
body:
The SOLACE+ consortium held its official kick-off meeting in Vienna on 25 November 2026, with 46 partners from 22 EU Member States and Norway taking part, according to the European Lung Foundation (ELF).

SOLACE+ builds on the original SOLACE project, which screened more than 30,000 people across 12 countries. The new project will strengthen screening implementation, learning, uptake and sustainability in 19 countries over the coming years, ELF said.

Scientific Coordinators Professor Rozemarijn Vliegenthart and Professor Torsten Blum opened the meeting with an overview of the project's objectives, structure and key timelines. The project aims to establish evidence, implementation frameworks and quality standards to help European countries launch and sustain effective lung cancer screening programmes.

Dr Debora Fumagalli (HaDEA, SOLACE Project Officer) and Dr Daniele Fiorenza (EC DG SANTE Policy Officer) presented the European Commission's perspective and expectations, underscoring the importance of the work within the EU's Beating Cancer Plan.

All nine work package leads gave presentations on how the consortium will approach different aspects of screening implementation. A dedicated session covered data management, the data platform, and ethical and legal aspects. Over the one-day meeting, partners exchanged ideas, defined priorities and aligned their efforts.

SOLACE+ is co-funded by the European Union's EU4Health programme under Grant Agreement No. 101314323.
key_quote: The project aims to establish robust evidence, implementation frameworks, and quality standards that will enable European countries to launch and sustain effective lung cancer screening programmes.

source.title: SOLACE+ consortium gathers in Vienna to launch ambitious lung cancer screening project
